summary: Expose declared seat and mission resources as read-only references

replay.detail: Existing declared-resource edges are folded into an indexed projection in bounded resumable batches after durable store open. Reference reads fall back to declarations until folding completes; API availability does not wait for the full fold. Empty stores complete the projection during open, and completed projections do not schedule background writer commits.

schema.detail: Adds the declared_resource_edges projection table, target index, declaration-maintenance triggers and resumable backfill metadata without changing the numeric database schema version.

rules.detail: Changes the shared-projection layout identity to st3.shared-projections.slo-breach-episodes-declared-resource-edges.v1 and includes declared resource edges in projection digests. Numeric checkpoint rules are unchanged. Older nodes continue exchanging claim authority but skip projection comparison until upgraded.

compatibility.detail: Adds optional read-only resources to seat and mission client models, GET /v1/resource-references/{subject}, and st subject show --references. Older daemons may omit resources. Regenerated clients retain current-main fields alongside the typed reference discriminator. Synthesized URI declarations have no accountable person. A single resource-aware desired-tree serializer serves agent onboarding, start, relocation, print-KDL and read/republication paths; generic rendering also preserves resource edges, using subject fallback without URI context. Explicit subject edges remain explicit. Cross-version client and daemon pairs have not been exercised.

downtime.detail: Durable projection backfill runs after open in bounded batches with declaration-backed reads during recovery. Restart-to-API and restart-to-health durations have not been measured for existing installations.

manual.detail: No manual declaration migration is required; authored resource names and reasons are preserved and shared URI targets remain reference-only rather than owned seats.

recovery.detail: Backfill stops with its owning store after the current bounded transaction rather than extending writer teardown through the entire backlog, and resumes from the last committed cursor after interruption. A failed background step logs a warning and reference reads continue from declarations. Binary swap-back across the new projection layout and schema objects has not been verified; prefer rolling forward and retain a pre-upgrade backup.
